# Judges Chapter 14 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_283.jpg, JDG_page_284.jpg

1. Samson went down to Timnah, and at Timnah he saw one of the daughters of the Philistines.

2. Then he came up and told his father and mother, "I saw one of the daughters of the Philistines at Timnah. Now get her for me as my wife."

3. But his father and mother said to him, "Is there not a woman among the daughters of your relatives, or among all our people, that you must go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes."

4. His father and mother did not know that it was from the LORD, for he was seeking an opportunity against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.

5. Then Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah, and they came to the vineyards of Timnah. And behold, a young lion came roaring toward him.

6. Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and although he had nothing in his hand, he tore the lion in pieces as one tears a young goat. But he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.

7. Then he went down and talked with the woman, and she was right in Samson's eyes.

8. After some days he returned to take her. And he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

9. He scraped it out into his hands and went on, eating as he went. And he came to his father and mother and gave some to them, and they ate. But he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey from the body of the lion.

10. His father went down to the woman, and Samson prepared a feast there, for so the young men used to do.

11. As soon as the people saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.

12. And Samson said to them, "Let me now put a riddle to you. If you can tell me what it is, within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.

13. But if you cannot tell me what it is, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." And they said to him, "Put your riddle, that we may hear it."

14. And he said to them, "Out of the eater came something to eat. Out of the strong came something sweet." And in three days they could not solve the riddle.

15. On the fourth day they said to Samson's wife, "Entice your husband to tell us what the riddle is, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire. Have you invited us here to impoverish us?"

16. And Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me; you do not love me. You have put a riddle to my people, and you have not told me what it is." And he said to her, "Behold, I have not told my father nor my mother, and shall I tell you?"

17. She wept before him the seven days that their feast lasted, and on the seventh day he told her, because she pressed him hard. Then she told the riddle to her people.

18. And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle."

19. And the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men of the town and took their spoil and gave the garments to those who had told the riddle. In hot anger he went back to his father's house.

20. And Samson's wife was given to his companion, who had been his best man.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 14 is Samson unbound — a man of tremendous physical power and no self-control. Every scene involves desire: desire for a woman (v.1), desire to show off (v.12), desire for revenge (v.19). The lion episode is the Samson cycle in miniature: he tears a lion apart but can't resist going back to look at it, then can't resist making it into a riddle, then can't resist telling the answer when pressed. Each "can't resist" leads to the next catastrophe.

**Verse 15 — "fourth" vs. "seventh":** The MT reads "seventh day" but this contradicts v.17 ("she wept the seven days"). LOGOS follows the LXX reading "fourth day." The consensus adopts "fourth" as the more coherent reading, noting the MT variant.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### v.3 — "she is right in my eyes" vs. "she looks good to me"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "she is right in my eyes" | ki-hi yashrah b'einai |
| LOGOS | "she is right in my eyes" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "She looks good to me" | Dynamic — "right" as visual attraction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew yashar b'einai means "right/straight in my eyes" — the same phrase used of Israel in 17:6 and 21:25 ("everyone did what was right in his own eyes"). This verbal echo is deliberate: Samson, the judge, does exactly what lawless Israel does. PNEUMA's "looks good to me" reduces a thematic keyword to mere physical attraction.

**Status:** Major. Thematic keyword connecting Samson to Israel's moral collapse.

---

### v.6 — "the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him" vs. "the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the Spirit of YHWH rushed upon him" | vatitslach alav ruach YHWH — tsalach |
| LOGOS | "the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him" | Generic + "powerfully" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew tsalach means "to rush/rush mightily upon" — it is Samson's distinctive Spirit-verb (14:6, 14:19, 15:14). It suggests sudden, overwhelming, almost violent empowerment. PNEUMA's "came powerfully upon" is vague — it could describe any of the Spirit-verbs in Judges. The specificity of "rushed" is essential for distinguishing Samson's Spirit-experience from Othniel's (hayah, "was upon"), Gideon's (lavash, "clothed"), and Jephthah's (hayah, "was upon").

**Status:** Major. Fifth Spirit-vocabulary entry — tsalach is unique to Samson and must be preserved.

---

### v.15 — "On the seventh day" vs. "On the fourth day"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "on the seventh day" | bayyom hashvi'i — follows MT |
| LOGOS | "On the fourth day" | Follows LXX, better narrative logic |
| PNEUMA | "On the fourth day" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The MT reads "seventh day" but this creates a contradiction with v.17 ("she wept the seven days"). If the threat was made on the seventh day, how could she weep for seven days? The LXX reads "fourth day" (bayyom harvi'i), which gives her three days of weeping before the seventh-day deadline. The consensus follows the LXX as the more coherent reading, noting the MT variant.

**Status:** Moderate. Textual variant — MT vs. LXX.

---

## Summary of Disagreement Patterns

| Pattern | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Thematic keyword loss | 1 | "Right in my eyes" → "looks good to me" (v.3) |
| Spirit-vocabulary | 1 | tsalach "rushed upon" → "came powerfully upon" (v.6) |
| Textual variant | 1 | "Seventh" (MT) vs. "fourth" (LXX) in v.15 |

**Overall pattern:** Chapter 14's most important disagreement is v.3 — the phrase "right in my eyes" (yashar b'einai) is a deliberate echo of the book's closing refrain (17:6, 21:25). PNEUMA's "looks good to me" severs this connection. The Spirit-vocabulary issue (v.6) continues the running disagreement: PNEUMA uses a generic phrase where the Hebrew employs a specific verb unique to Samson.

---

*— SOPHIA, AI Translator, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
